analysis:
Only docs/architecture/inference.md changed (date bump, GLM video frame-timing wording, and new GLM5-Next logprob/output-control text at head 1732-1751 plus a new section around head 876-895). The two supplied units (head lines 1225-2032) are unchanged surrounding documentation, except the head 1732-1751 range, which is the new native-tracked-engine paragraph. No code, config, auth, crypto or protocol surface is altered by this PR.

Security-relevant claims in the new text: a native-tracked engine (GLM5-Next, MiMo V2.6) refuses token constraints and unqualified topLogprobs rows. EngineV2Bridge.nativeOutputControlRefusal rejects them first as a 400 client_error, before any reservation, so a consumer cannot trigger the provider-fault 500 generation_failure that strikes the coordinator's inference-error breaker. That is an availability-hardening statement (related to ADV-002 and TB-002 DoS), consistent with the threat model. I did not see the code, so I cannot verify it. The GLM logprob rows are described as sampling through the ordinary sampler, never drafting, and forcing target-only decode for a step. That is a performance characteristic with no confidentiality impact.

The cache and prefix-cache statements in these units (SSD checkpoint, encrypted prefix state, T-041) are descriptive and do not loosen the TTL, the adoption gate, the HMAC lookup or the account scoping. The prompt-cache identity is stated unchanged by the sampler. The VFR video change (indexed rather than refused) in the earlier range is outside these units. Remaining question: whether the corresponding code changes, not supplied here, behave as documented. The doc-only diff here creates no regression.
